Base Threat: Azure IoT Hub connection string is stored in .env file on IoTEdge Device. Once user gains access to the device, .env file can be read and attacker cause Dos attacks on IoTHub
Model Threat: A malicious actor obtains an IoT Edge module’s credentials or identity (e.g., via stolen deployment credentials or misconfigured IoT Hub identities) and registers a fake IoT Edge device or EdgeRuntime that appears legitimate to Azure IoT Hub. Unauthorized device can receive configuration and secrets (connection strings) and send falsified telemetry to Application Insights, undermining trust in monitoring and potentially exposing sensitive configuration data.

Base Threat: Application Insights is connected via Connection String which is stored in .env file on the IoTEdge device. Once user gains access to the device, .env file can be read and attacker can tamper the log data.
Model Threat: A malicious actor tampers with telemetry sent to Azure Application Insights or Azure Monitor (e.g., by altering metric values or log contents in the sending modules) to hide abnormal behavior or fabricate normal operation. Security and operational monitoring becomes untrustworthy; attacks, performance issues, or data leaks may go undetected or be misdiagnosed, increasing dwell time and damage.

Base Threat: Unauthorized Access to M2 IoTEdge Module where database secrets are used
Model Threat: If WebSocket connections between M1, M2, and M3 on the public-access LAN are not encrypted, an attacker with LAN access can sniff network traffic and reconstruct live video frames, OCR text, and scan results as they traverse the network. Exposure of confidential video content, order information, and potentially personal or sensitive data, leading to privacy violations and regulatory non-compliance.

Base Threat: Dos attack on all IoTEdge Modules since there is no Authentication
Model Threat: An attacker on the local network sends a flood of HTTP requests to M1’s public-access LAN endpoint from multiple machines, exhausting CPU, memory, or network resources on the IoT Edge device. Legitimate users lose access to live video streaming and order scanning functionality; the IoT Edge device may become unstable or unresponsive, disrupting business operations relying on real-time processing.
